 Judgment

This appeal has been filed by the third respondent insurer in OP(MV) No.844 of 2005 on the file of the Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Pathanamthitta, challenging the liability to pay compensation awarded by the tribunal.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Pathanamthitta
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondents 1 to 3 herein were the claimant and respondents 1 & 2 before the tribunal.

2. The case of the claimant was that on 19.03.2005, while he was travelling in a toyota tempo bearing Reg.No.KL-07-C-4251 along the Pathanapuram-Kayamkulam public road driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner, it hit behind a lorry, whereby he sustained serious injuries.
The claimant approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 3,88,000/-.
3. Respondents 1 and 2, the driver and owner of the offending vehicle respectively, remained ex parte before the tribunal.
The third respondent insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy coverage for the vehicle, but disputing the liability and quantum of compensation claimed.
PW1 & PW2 were examined and Exts.A1 to A11 & B1 were marked.

The tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and 2025:KER:87509 ..3..
materials on record, held that the accident took place on account of the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and awarded a sum of 3,45,275/- as compensation under different heads with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of petition till realization against the third respondent being the insurer with right of recovery against the owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondent insurer has come up in appeal, challenging its liability to pay compensation.
4. Heard the learned Standing Counsel for the appellant/insurer and the learned counsel for the first respondent/claimant.
Though notice was served on the third respondent/owner of the offending vehicle, he has not chosen to appear.

5. The learned Standing Counsel for the insurer submits that the claimant was a gratuitous passenger in the goods vehicle and the policy issued was an "act only" policy and no additional premium was paid for the passengers in the goods vehicle, however, the tribunal directed the insurer to pay the compensation to the claimant and then, to recover from the owner of the offending vehicle.

According to the learned Standing Counsel, since the policy issued to the vehicle was an "act only" policy, there is no liability for the insurer to indemnify the insured and to pay compensation to the claimant.

To substantiate the 2025:KER:87509 ..4..
said contention, the learned Standing Counsel for the insurer relied on United India Insurance Co.
Ltd. v. Tilak Singh [2006 (2) KLT 884 (SC)].
National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Rajesh on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155464368/
2 6.

sentences.text: During the course of the argument, the learned Standing Counsel handed over to me a copy of Ext.B1 policy, a perusal of which shows that it is an "act only" policy and no additional premium was paid for the passengers travelling in the vehicle.

This Court, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Ummalimma [2025 KHC OnLine 902], held that if the policy is "act only" policy and no additional premium is paid to cover the passengers of the vehicle, the policy will not cover the gratuitous passengers in the said vehicle; and the insurer is not liable to pay compensation; and if the insurer is not liable to pay compensation, then, there shall not be a direction to 'pay and recover'; and in all cases, such order of 'pay and recover' would not arise when the insurer is not liable but would, in the facts and circumstances, be considered by the court to meet the ends of justice.
7.

entities.text:
National Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Ummalimma [2025 KHC OnLine 902]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, following the judgments in Tilak Singh (supra) and Ummalimma (supra), I hold that the policy being an "act only"
policy, the insurer is not liable to pay the amount awarded and the direction of the tribunal to the insurer to pay compensation and then, to 2025:KER:87509 ..5..
recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle is legally unsustainable and is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
The impugned order of the tribunal to the extent of directing the insurer to pay compensation to the claimant and then, to recover from the owner of the offending vehicle is hereby set aside.
It is made clear that the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation awarded by the tribunal.

SD/-
SHOBA ANNAMMA EAPEN JUDGE bka/-
